items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut large language model prices by up to 80% over several months amid competitive pressure [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI and Anthropic have significantly reduced the prices of their large language models (LLMs) by up to 80% since June 2026, with multiple price cuts announced for various models including GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5. These reductions have occurred alongside new model releases and improvements in performance, with cache read costs-a major expense in agentic coding-also being lowered substantially. The timeline shows a pattern of competitive responses between the two companies, with price cuts often following each other's announcements. Despite the steep discounts, the models have maintained or improved output quality. The reductions reflect both technological advances and strategic pricing moves in a rapidly evolving AI market, where improved model capabilities are driving increased usage even as costs per token decline.

items.title: IBM CEO says open weight AI models now deliver 90% of frontier model performance at 10% cost for on-premises use [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna stated that open weight AI models have become highly effective and cost-efficient for on-premises enterprise deployment, offering about 90% of the performance of leading closed models at roughly 10% of the token cost. He highlighted that this shift is driving strong interest in on-prem AI infrastructure, which can be built in just two or three racks but requires specialized engineering expertise to optimize performance and deployment. Krishna noted that while some tasks may still require the highest-performing models, most enterprise applications like email summarization, contract analysis, and customer support can be handled well by these more affordable open models. IBM plans to support this trend by developing software to simplify AI deployments and expects increased sales of its Spyre mainframe accelerator cards. The company also reported modest growth in infrastructure and software revenue, with Red Hat showing strong performance in virtualization products.

items.title: Apollo says AI has delivered zero financial returns outside the technology sector, highlighting limited economic impact in other industries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Apollo Global Management stated that artificial intelligence has not yet produced any financial gains outside the technology industry. The firm noted that despite notable AI advancements, the economic benefits remain confined primarily to the tech sector at this time.

items.title: Researchers propose attention-free Grassmann flow architecture for sequence modeling, achieving competitive results with fewer parameters compared to Transformers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A new study challenges the necessity of explicit self-attention in sequence modeling by introducing a novel attention-free architecture based on Grassmann flows. This approach encodes local token pairs as two-dimensional subspaces on a Grassmann manifold and propagates information through controlled deformations of low-rank subspaces, offering a more structured and interpretable alternative to traditional multi-head attention mechanisms. The proposed Causal Grassmann layer reduces token states linearly and fuses geometric features back into hidden states via gated mixing. On benchmarks like Wikitext-2 and SNLI, models using this method with 13 to 18 million parameters achieve validation perplexities and accuracies close to or slightly better than size-matched Transformers. The research highlights linear scaling in sequence length and suggests manifold-based designs could advance geometric and invariant-based neural reasoning.

items.title: The Economist says AI displacement of workers risks loss of social connections, purpose, and mental well-being beyond income [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Economist discusses the broader consequences of artificial intelligence potentially displacing human workers, emphasizing that the impact extends beyond lost wages to include diminished social ties, sense of purpose, and mental health. The article highlights the importance of considering these non-monetary effects when addressing AI's impact on employment. It explores how work provides more than financial support, serving as a source of identity and community for many individuals. The piece suggests that policies and responses to AI-driven job displacement should account for these deeper human needs to mitigate negative outcomes effectively.

items.title: Authentic Brands Group sues Anthropic for using 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI models without permission, seeking $41 million in damages [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Authentic Brands Group, which owns the rights to Elvis Presley's music and likeness, has filed a lawsuit against AI company Anthropic for allegedly using 274 of Presley's songs to train its AI model Claude without authorization. The lawsuit claims this use infringes on copyrights and seeks $150,000 per track, totaling about $41 million. The complaint alleges that Anthropic's AI has produced infringing outputs from nearly every song catalog available online and that the company knowingly continued copyright infringement despite implementing ineffective guardrails. This case marks one of the first major legal challenges directly from an artist's estate against an AI developer and could set a precedent for how AI companies use existing music catalogs.

items.title: Ask HN: Companies discuss whether human review is required for AI-generated code before integration [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A Hacker News discussion asks if companies mandate human review of AI-generated code prior to integration. Participants report varied practices, with some requiring thorough human oversight to ensure code quality and security, while others apply more flexible approaches depending on the use case and confidence in AI tools.

items.title: Nodecode launches open-source Lisp-based living agent that rewrites its own code and evolves autonomously [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Nodecode is an open-source project featuring a living agent written in Lisp that can rewrite and update its own code while running, enabling continuous evolution and adaptability. It operates as a single process in SBCL, with multiple clients connecting to the same running instance, and supports self-updating definitions managed via git. The agent uses a unique approach where code is treated as data, allowing it to evaluate and keep new Lisp definitions dynamically. Nodecode supports modular extensions called cells, which add new capabilities such as chat rooms, tools, or integrations. It also manages its context by retaining and recalling previous states without losing information. Nodecode claims efficiency advantages in token usage compared to other coding agents on public ARC-AGI-3 benchmark games. It runs on user-provided AI models and is available under the MIT license for Linux, macOS, and Windows platforms.

items.title: RainbowSay launches platform for live language learning and teaching through interactive shows with real-time practice and gentle corrections
items.content_text: RainbowSay offers a platform that turns users' favorite shows into language lessons by providing vocabulary and grammar support for every sentence. Learners can practice speaking aloud and receive gentle corrections, with features like streaks and heatmaps to track progress. The platform aims to make language learning engaging by integrating it with entertainment content users already enjoy.

items.title: Clivern launches Sloth gateway for AI agents, APIs, and MCP servers with service discovery, load balancing, and health checks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Clivern has introduced Sloth, an open-source gateway and service discovery registry designed to unify access and management for AI agents, APIs, and MCP servers. Sloth enables registration and discovery of AI agents and routes calls through a single gateway that manages load balancing, health checks, and policy enforcement. Sloth follows Semantic Versioning for predictable releases and backward compatibility, with changelogs and roadmaps available on its GitHub repository. The project encourages community contributions and provides channels for bug reports and security issue disclosures.

items.title: Depono launches platform to chat with multiple AI models at 10% cost, storing files with Git version control [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Depono is a platform that enables users to interact with multiple AI models simultaneously while reducing costs to 10% of typical rates. The service also integrates file storage using Git for version control and management, providing a streamlined experience for managing AI interactions and data.

items.title: Anthropic prepares to file IPO paperwork with details on finances, ownership, revenue sources, and governance expected [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic is expected to publicly file its initial public offering paperwork soon, revealing more about its financial trajectory, ownership structure, revenue sources, and corporate governance. The filing may clarify how much Anthropic pays cloud providers like Google and Amazon, the concentration of its revenue among key customers, and the voting power arrangements among its founders and board members. The IPO filing comes amid broader tech industry events, including upcoming earnings reports from major cloud providers Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, and news of Instacart exploring a potential sale. These developments are likely to influence market perceptions of AI demand and cloud infrastructure spending.

items.title: Nvidia partners with German firm to explore converting decommissioned nuclear plants into AI data centers using existing infrastructure [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Nvidia has entered a preliminary partnership with German energy company PreussenElektra GmbH to assess the feasibility of repurposing shut-down nuclear power plant sites in Germany into high-performance AI data centers. The project focuses on leveraging existing power, water, and industrial infrastructure at these sites without using nuclear power for the data centers themselves. The exploration will evaluate the sites' energy grid connections, land availability, and infrastructure to meet the operational requirements of AI data centers, aiming to reduce costs and development time compared to building new facilities from scratch. Germany permanently shut down its last nuclear plants in April 2023, and PreussenElektra is currently dismantling several sites that could be considered for this initiative, which remains in an experimental feasibility phase with no finalized investments or construction plans.

items.title: Grok releases first seven minutes of its AI-generated Odyssey series, following Elon Musk's announcement [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Grok has published the first seven minutes of its AI-generated adaptation of The Odyssey, marking the debut episode of its planned series. This release follows Elon Musk's earlier claim that Grok would produce a full-length, historically accurate movie version of the classic epic. The AI-generated footage, created in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker, features Musk-approved casting choices and a British-accented narration. While some scenes approximate realism, the overall presentation lacks artistic depth, momentum, and emotional engagement compared to Christopher Nolan's recent film adaptation, which was a major box office success. The initial episode has received mixed reactions, with viewers noting its technical competence but questioning its ability to sustain interest over a full-length feature. Grok has invited feedback and offered to provide a detailed breakdown of the production process.

items.title: Biff releases version 2.0.4 with new large language model skills including code review and specification implementation tools [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Biff version 2.0.4 introduces a set of large language model (LLM) skills designed to assist with software development tasks such as reading specifications, generating implementation plans, reviewing code against Biff-specific conventions, and improving code quality. These skills integrate into the development workflow to automate and enhance coding processes. The update includes specific tools like biff-spec-review for planning, biff-spec-dev for implementation, and biff-code-review for enforcing coding standards. The code review skill uses explicit rules and a checklist system to identify and fix violations, allowing for human oversight if needed. Users can upgrade their biff.tasks dependency to access these features, which aim to improve the quality and consistency of LLM-generated code in Biff projects.

items.title: GOD launches real-time control room for managing large language model agent societies, demoed at EMNLP 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: GOD is a new system demonstrated at EMNLP 2026 that provides a real-time control room for overseeing and interacting with societies of large language model (LLM) agents. It allows users to replay runs, query individual agents, intervene in their actions, and export experiment packs from a single interface. The platform supports no-code setup via a browser wizard, pluggable map and agent packages, bilingual UI, and runs locally with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It aims to facilitate inspection and experimentation with LLM agent societies rather than simulate realistic social behavior. The project is open source and offers a public site with browser-based replays and downloadable experiments.

items.title: AI company develops complex internal roles and processes, prompting consideration of formal HR functions as it grows operationally real [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: An AI-driven synthetic company has evolved from a simple workflow of AI systems into a complex organization with distinct roles, departments, and internal procedures, leading its CEO to consider establishing a Human Resources department. The company now includes specialized AI roles such as architects, marketers, editors, and software engineers, each with defined responsibilities and governance protocols, reflecting the structure of a traditional business. This organizational growth has introduced challenges like role proliferation, operational confusion, and the need for formal communication and governance, exemplified by the creation of a company name and internal memos. The CEO observes that the synthetic company is becoming operationally real despite lacking physical employee needs, highlighting the increasing complexity of managing AI-driven workflows and the potential necessity for HR-like oversight.

items.title: Germany plans to repurpose idle nuclear power plants as AI data centers amid energy transition
items.content_text: Germany is exploring the conversion of its idle nuclear power plants into AI data centers to leverage existing infrastructure and support the growing demand for data processing. This initiative aims to utilize the plants' robust power supply and cooling capabilities to meet the energy-intensive needs of AI workloads. The plan reflects Germany's efforts to balance energy transition goals with technological advancement by finding new uses for decommissioned nuclear facilities.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic models solve multiple longstanding mathematical problems, demonstrating new AI capabilities in complex proofs and conjectures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Recent AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic have solved several longstanding open mathematical problems, including a counterexample to Erdős's unit distance conjecture and proofs related to the Cycle Double Cover problem and Navier-Stokes equations. These advances highlight AI's growing proficiency in mathematical reasoning and problem solving. The models approach problem solving differently from humans, using depth-first search strategies and leveraging extensive pretraining to reduce the effort needed for insights. This shift in search patterns allows AI to tackle complex problems more efficiently, potentially changing how mathematical research and discovery are conducted in the future.

items.title: DuckDB developers detail eight security risks and mitigation strategies for running DuckDB servers in production environments
items.content_text: The article outlines security challenges when deploying DuckDB as a shared server, where SQL users are treated as the operating system user by default. It identifies eight classes of exposure, including credential leaks through environment variables, command lines, and persistent secrets, and explains how these can be exploited by SQL users to access unauthorized data or settings. The author describes practical solutions such as using temporary secrets files, disabling persistent secrets loading, and restricting filesystem access to prevent unauthorized data exposure. The article also explains how the Quack on Demand system implements these protections by default, including a gateway that validates SQL statements before they reach DuckDB nodes, ensuring safer multi-user deployments.

items.title: Xflops integrates Flame Serving with standalone vLLM, achieving near-parity in throughput and improving cache reuse for large language model inference [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Xflops has advanced the integration of Flame Serving with standalone vLLM to enhance the efficiency of serving large language models. Their experiments show that after tuning, Flame's median completion throughput is within 0.86% of standalone vLLM, meeting a target of at least 99% of reference throughput across most workloads. This integration aims to bring the benefits of Flame Serving, such as improved cache reuse and batch processing, closer to the standalone vLLM environment. The team conducted matched experiments using two B200 GPUs and the BF16 Llama 3.1 8B Instruct model, comparing standalone vLLM with a Flame Python service embedding vLLM. They found that persistent worker placement and techniques like asynchronous engine admission and lossless input compression helped close the performance gap. Both systems benefited from prefix affinity, which increased throughput by over 70% by enabling reuse of cached token data. These results apply to short, finite bursts rather than continuous workloads and do not yet demonstrate an advantage from Flame's data-aware scheduler.

items.title: OpenSparta launches AI agent to automate customer discovery and engagement on Telegram with account and proxy management [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenSparta has developed an AI agent that automates finding relevant conversations and posting contextual comments on Telegram to help users discover new audiences. The platform manages Telegram accounts and proxies from a single workspace, ensuring account health and compliance with Telegram's safety limits. Users can start for free and preview paid modules before purchasing, enabling automated Telegram engagement without manual intervention.

items.title: Bend launches a fast programming language with formal proofs to block AI errors and enforce app correctness [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Bend is a new programming language designed to improve AI system reliability by requiring formal proofs that enforce application rules, preventing bugs from being merged. It compiles as fast as C on CPUs and CUDA on GPUs, supports parallel execution, and verifies proofs in under a second, making correctness guarantees practical for AI-generated code. The language uses a special LAWS.bend file where developers declare rules their app must follow, and the compiler demands mathematical proofs that these laws hold whenever code changes. This approach blocks AI mistakes by forcing retries until no rules are violated, ensuring apps behave as intended without manual code review. Bend targets backend development on Linux and macOS and aims to replace ambiguous natural language with precise, provable intents for AI-driven software construction.

items.title: New 3D mesh playground launched for coding agents using three.js and manifold-3d [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A new platform enables developers to code and interact with agents within a 3D mesh environment, leveraging three.js and manifold-3d technologies. This playground offers a hands-on experience for those interested in 3D graphics and agent-based programming.

items.title: Purifi launches a shared live canvas platform integrating humans and agentic AI for real-time financial analysis and decision-making without building AI models from scratch [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Purifi has introduced a collaborative platform that allows multiple users and agentic AI to work together on a single live canvas, integrating financial data, market information, documents, and tools in real time. This environment enables teams to analyze, question assumptions, generate insights, and produce reports without the need for separate meetings or installations. The platform supports features such as on-demand cash-flow and relative valuation models, options structuring, SEC filings analysis, voice-driven research, and portfolio review automation. Purifi partners with major cloud and AI infrastructure providers like Microsoft Azure and IBM, emphasizing that users can compete in AI-driven financial work by leveraging existing AI capabilities rather than building models from scratch.

items.title: Glitchrupt launches a macOS tool that glitches the desktop to notify users when their AI agent needs attention [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Glitchrupt is a macOS application that visually glitches the desktop with brief pixel fractures and digital static to alert users when their AI agent requires input. The tool runs on macOS 14 or later, overlays effects on all displays without saving or transmitting data, and supports customizable sound cues and repeated reminders until the agent's request is resolved. It integrates with AI agents like Codex via a local server and command-line interface, allowing users to manage notifications and approval workflows while maintaining control over the alerts.

items.title: Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI advises against AI labs designating specific mathematicians for early access to AI-generated outputs due to risks of bias, unequal access, and reduced community agency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence has recommended that AI labs avoid assigning particular mathematicians early access to AI-generated mathematical results. They argue this practice can delay or restrict access for others, bias the selection process, and limit the mathematical community's agency in interpreting and developing understanding of the outputs. The group emphasizes that human understanding of AI-generated work can develop organically when materials are released publicly and encourages community-led engagement instead. The group highlights several disadvantages of designated mathematicians, including potential conflicts of interest, the risk of their reputations being used to shield AI companies from criticism, and the opaque nature of selection processes that may not align with community priorities. They suggest AI labs follow alternative release pathways that promote transparency, broad access, and adherence to scholarly standards, fostering a more inclusive and accountable approach to disseminating AI-generated mathematical research.

items.title: Apollo economist says AI delivers zero financial payoff to most non-tech S&P 500 companies, with flat profit margins and productivity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Apollo Global Management's chief economist Torsten Slok reports that artificial intelligence has not improved profit margins or revenue per worker for most large corporations outside the major tech firms in the S&P 500. He highlights that despite significant investments and hype, AI has yet to boost productivity or financial returns in corporate America beyond the tech sector. Slok analyzed the S&P 493, excluding Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla, and expressed skepticism about non-tech companies' ability to convert AI advancements into higher revenue growth and profit margins. He noted that AI lacks understanding of accountability, trust, culture, and ethical considerations, which are crucial for driving business success. Recent studies also support the finding that AI has not yet delivered significant productivity gains across industries.

items.title: TechCrunch lists notable AI wearables including Amazon's Bee, Friend, Limitless, Meta's Muse Charm, Nirva, Omi, and Plaud NotePin with features from conversation recording to emotional support [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A variety of AI-powered wearables are emerging to integrate artificial intelligence into daily life, offering functions from productivity tools to emotional companionship. Devices like Amazon's Bee pendant and wristbands record conversations and create reminders, while Friend provides emotional support with mood recognition and proactive messaging. Meta's upcoming Muse Charm features a digital avatar assistant, and Nirva focuses on personal growth by analyzing speech patterns. Other devices include Limitless, which transcribes and summarizes conversations for professionals, Omi, which uses ChatGPT to provide personalized advice, and Plaud's NotePin, a wearable voice recorder with AI transcription aimed at students and professionals. These products vary in price and capabilities, reflecting a growing market for AI wearables designed to assist with communication, organization, and emotional well-being.

items.title: UC Berkeley math professor stops grading homework due to widespread AI use among students, citing AI's growing capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Richard Borcherds, a UC Berkeley math professor and Fields medalist, has ceased grading homework for correctness after observing extensive AI use by students to achieve top scores. He now grades only on completion, acknowledging the system's limitations and the inevitability of AI assistance in coursework. Borcherds expressed uncertainty about the future of mathematics careers as AI advances, noting that AI recently solved a major unsolved math problem and may soon surpass human mathematicians in capability. The Berkeley Academic Senate recommends faculty include AI use policies in course syllabi, but enforcement varies by course. The university has tested AI detection tools like Turnitin and Rumi but found them inadequate for standard use. Faculty retain discretion over AI policies, supported by resources such as the AI Hub, which offers sample statements and training materials. Borcherds highlighted the inertia in academic systems despite technological shifts, comparing the current situation to past disruptions in other industries.

items.title: Reddit's r/opensource bans AI-related projects, non-English posts, and new solo developer submissions in updated rules [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The moderators of Reddit's r/opensource subreddit have implemented new submission rules that ban projects using AI, projects made by AI, or intended for AI, citing incompatibility with the community's open source values. The rules also require projects to be at least one year old, actively maintained, and have multiple contributors, effectively barring new solo developers from seeking help. Additionally, non-English speakers are discouraged from participating due to concerns about verifying AI-generated translations.

items.title: Google's AI search features disrupt online publishing by reducing traffic to news sites and changing search result rankings [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google's introduction of AI-powered search features, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, has significantly altered the online publishing landscape by decreasing traffic to many news outlets. These AI features summarize content at the top of search results, often reducing user clicks to original publisher websites, which has raised concerns among publishers and media organizations worldwide. Since the rollout of these AI search tools, several major publishers such as Business Insider, The Washington Post, and The New York Times have reported notable declines in search-driven traffic. Despite Google's claims that AI search benefits the web ecosystem, data from analytics firms and trade associations indicate substantial drops in click-through rates, prompting lawsuits and regulatory scrutiny. Publishers are now adapting by shifting focus to social media, newsletters, and subscription models to sustain their audiences and revenue.

items.title: Poll shows 57% of Americans believe AI is bad for society, with 17% viewing it as extremely harmful amid rising cybersecurity and job loss concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent poll conducted by the Washington Post, ABC News, and IPSOS found that 57 percent of Americans consider AI harmful to society, while only 42 percent see it as beneficial. The survey of over 2,500 adults revealed that 17 percent view AI as extremely bad, compared to just 2 percent who see it as extremely good, reflecting growing public skepticism amid reports of AI-related cybersecurity threats and job displacement risks. The poll also highlighted demographic and political divides, with 65 percent of Americans under 30 and 63 percent of Democrats viewing AI negatively, compared to 51 percent of Republicans. Additionally, 73 percent of respondents expressed high concern over AI hacking secure systems, and 66 percent opposed new data center construction in the US, indicating widespread apprehension about AI's societal impact and infrastructure demands.

items.title: Super Smash Bros creator Masahiro Sakurai criticizes AI-generated games as derivative and unoriginal, warning of an overwhelming influx on platforms like Steam [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Masahiro Sakurai, creator of Super Smash Bros and Kirby, criticized the use of AI in video game development, saying it leads to a flood of derivative and low-quality titles that prioritize speed over originality. He expressed concern that AI-generated games will dominate platforms like Steam, making it difficult to track or appreciate new releases. Sakurai highlighted that AI tends to replicate existing game systems and styles, exacerbating a trend of unoriginality in the industry. He contrasted AI's limitations with human creativity, emphasizing that unique artistic visions, such as those from creators like Fumito Ueda, cannot be replicated by AI.

items.title: Researchers say ChatGPT builds detailed psychological profiles of users through memory retention, raising privacy concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A study by researchers from Germany, India, and the Netherlands found that ChatGPT retains extensive user information to create personalized digital profiles, including psychological insights, based on private conversations. The analysis of chat logs from 80 users revealed that 96% of memory entries were created by the chatbot without explicit user control, with 28% containing personal data under GDPR standards and 52% revealing psychological details. The researchers warn that this form of personalization poses new privacy risks as users may treat chatbots like friends or advisors, sharing sensitive information. They highlight concerns that such detailed profiling could reinforce biases and political polarization, especially since the chatbot's memory system can make assumptions about users. While OpenAI has updated its memory system and allows users to opt out, the study emphasizes the need for closer examination of these mechanisms and their broader implications.

items.title: Microsoft says its new AI diagnostic model outperforms generalist physicians in accuracy and cost efficiency in controlled study [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Microsoft's AI Diagnostic Orchestrator (MAI-DxO) demonstrated over twice the diagnostic accuracy of generalist physicians in a peer-reviewed study published in Science, achieving 83.2% accuracy on clinical case reports and 80.3% on emergency department cases. The AI also reduced diagnostic costs to half or a third of those incurred by human doctors by sequentially gathering information and ordering tests in a simulated environment. The study tested the AI's ability to diagnose patients without prior knowledge of all symptoms, mimicking a real clinical process by interacting with a gatekeeper agent that provided case information. While the results highlight AI's potential to improve healthcare delivery, Microsoft acknowledges that real-world application requires further validation, as human doctors perform additional roles such as patient interaction and information gathering beyond symptom analysis.

items.title: Report: America lost over 200,000 jobs in media, film, and arts over four years amid rise of AI-generated content [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: America has lost more than 200,000 jobs in creative industries such as media, film, and the arts over the past four years, with about 50,000 lost in the last year alone. This decline coincides with the rise of AI systems capable of producing novels, images, music, and other digital art at low cost, although the exact impact of AI on job losses is difficult to isolate due to other factors like industry consolidation and offshoring. Job losses have affected nearly every subsector of digital arts, with the movie and sound recording sector, including Hollywood, losing over 100,000 jobs-nearly one-third of its workforce-making it the hardest hit area. While in-person entertainment continues to grow, digital media sectors such as live broadcasting, streaming, and graphic design have experienced unusual downturns compared to previous years. The ongoing job losses raise questions about the future viability of traditional creative industry business models amid AI advancements.

items.content_text: ADRs4AI introduces a system that captures and versions the reasoning behind human-AI decisions in Git repositories, ensuring that the thought process and options considered during collaboration are preserved and accessible. The method involves AI generating Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) from user input, which include questions, options, recommendations, and rationale, allowing users to accept or override AI suggestions while maintaining a clear record of why decisions were made. The system supports a bitemporal hybrid model to track changes over time, combining Git history with explicit valid-time and observed-time metadata to handle corrections and updates without losing historical context. Designed for ease of use, it enables users to start recording deliberations quickly and supports collaborative workflows with multiple participants, aiming to reduce cognitive load and improve decision transparency in AI-assisted projects.

items.title: Apollo Chief Economist says AI has not improved revenue or profit margins outside the tech sector as of 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

Revenue per worker and profit margins have increased for the largest tech firms but remain flat for the broader S&P 493, with no signs of AI-driven productivity growth. Mainstream companies are beginning to view AI spending as a cost rather than a growth driver. The analysis highlights that venture-backed firms continue to invest heavily in AI tokens, but most corporations are reluctant to pay for the latest AI models. The report suggests that AI's impact on the wider economy will remain limited unless mainstream companies can leverage AI to boost revenue and margins, which may be challenging due to AI's lack of judgment, accountability, and understanding of complex business factors like trust and ethics. The ultimate effect of AI will be determined by its adoption and results in the broader market beyond the leading tech firms.

items.title: Study finds Grok AI favors Republican candidates in 92% of midterm races while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats in 97%, with less than 10% agreement across nearly 500 races [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

The study used API access to the models, which differ from their consumer chatbot versions that typically avoid direct endorsements. Researchers noted that Grok often cited conservative sources and focused on issues like immigration and taxes, whereas GPT relied on sources like Wikipedia and the Associated Press and emphasized healthcare and abortion. The study also highlighted potential hidden instructions in Grok's API requests that may influence its political leanings. OpenAI stated that its consumer-facing ChatGPT is designed to be neutral and does not provide voting recommendations, contrasting with the API behavior tested in the study. The findings raise concerns about implicit biases in AI models used for political information, as these biases could influence users indirectly through topic selection and framing even when direct candidate endorsements are avoided. Experts warn that such biases may affect public understanding and discourse around elections as AI tools become more common sources of information.

The IAM policies allow administrators to enforce read-only or restricted access by denying permissions for certain tools, applying controls at the organization, folder, or project level. While the skill guardrails rely on agent compliance, the IAM policies provide enforced security boundaries, though they currently only cover Google Cloud MCP servers and have some limitations in visibility and enforcement scope. Industry experts note that combining these guardrails with features like short-lived credentials and audit trails can enhance containment and governance. However, challenges remain around idempotency and handling retries in production environments. items.title: Why Blackstone Thinks AI Bottlenecks Could Work in its Favor [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Greetings! On their earnings calls earlier in the week, Meta Platforms and SpaceX delivered the same underlying message to investors: demand for AI is running ahead of the supply of AI compute. On Thursday, another important player in the AI ecosystem-Blackstone, the alternative asset management giant-repeated a version of that refrain. On its own earnings call, the firm, a major investor at the center of the AI data center boom, faced pointed questions from analysts about rising financing costs and mounting investor concerns over the sustainability of the buildout. Its executives argued that the very factors threatening the AI industry's expansion could actually work in Blackstone's favor. CEO Steve Schwarzman noted that constraints on power availability and growing public opposition to new data centers are making it harder to bring new capacity online, potentially making existing facilities more valuable. Blackstone President Jon Gray also suggested the firm could seek higher returns on projects where it hasn't signed leases yet in order to offset rising borrowing costs. Blackstone's third-quarter results offered some support for that argument: Its infrastructure investments were buoyed by what executives called "extraordinary" data center leasing momentum, significantly outperforming its broader private equity and real estate holdings. "Despite all the negative things you're reading about AI today, when we look across our business, this continues to be the area where we're driving the highest returns," Gray said during the call. But it's hard to ignore the fact that the financing concerns and roadblocks threatening the broader AI infrastructure buildout are also hitting closer to home for Blackstone. Fears about rising financing costs have sent CoreWeave's stock and bond prices plunging-the neocloud's shares closed down another 10% Thursday after sliding last week-while Australian AI cloud provider Firmus abruptly pulled its initial public offering earlier this month. Blackstone has provided billions in loans to CoreWeave and has both invested in and lent money to Firmus. Blackstone has also been pressing ahead with brand-new AI ventures. In May, the firm announced an initial $5 billion equity commitment to a joint venture with Google to create a new cloud company that will use Google's TPU chips, with plans to bring 500 megawatts of capacity online by next year. The venture could need as much as $25 billion in total investment, including some borrowed money, and it has reportedly encountered delays at potential data center sites. Blackstone, for its part, says that broader anxiety about AI hasn't undermined its ability to raise fresh cash for making its own investments. "We're continuing to be able to raise capital. Obviously investors are asking the same question around AI, but what we continue to see is demand and usage of the AI going up faster than the compute," Gray said. While Blackstone says it wants to continue going big in AI, it can only finance a tiny portion of the industry's broader infrastructure buildout itself. The trillions of dollars of financing needed for chips and data centers in the coming years requires raising money from a far broader pool of investors. Blackstone itself has said it's not clear where all the money will come from. Jas Khaira, the head of the team leading Blackstone's push into AI investment, said late last month that the firm is still trying to determine which investors across the public debt and private credit markets will be able to provide the funding needed to sustain the buildout. "We have not mapped out who's going to buy all the debt. We have some hypotheses, but the honest answer is we don't know where all of it will come from," he said at The Information's AI Agenda event in San Francisco. Data Center Headwinds Despite Blackstone's overall positive note on AI demand, we got fresh evidence Thursday afternoon of the uncertainty in the IPO market for companies in the data center business. Phoebe Liu and Valida Pau had a scoop that SB Energy, a company controlled by SoftBank Group that is developing an OpenAI data center in Ohio, is discussing a plan to put off its IPO until December or earlier next year. Previously, SB Energy was aiming to go public in September. items.title: Salesforce Customers Brace For New Fees to Use Claude in Its Apps [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Salesforce is leading the software industry's attempt to collect fees from businesses that use Claude and other external AI tools to automate work in enterprise apps. As soon as next month, Salesforce plans to require companies to register outside AI agents, a step toward charging them each time those agents update or analyze data stored in Salesforce. The fees let Salesforce earn money from customers who use such AI instead of paying for Salesforce's built-in AI products. The Salesforce tollgate has implications for the rest of the industry, which is coming to terms with the idea that so-called AI agents may be able to use software firms' apps more efficiently than humans do, meaning their seat-based or per-user pricing model might not have staying power. The question is whether the new AI tollgates-which Atlassian, Workday, ServiceNow and Datadog are also erecting to various extents-and other pricing shifts will more than make up for an eventual decline in per-seat subscription revenues. The vast majority of workers haven't yet outsourced such work to AI, of course, and companies like Salesforce are trying to get more revenue from them as well. They charge fees based on how much they use the apps' built-in AI tools and are also experimenting with outcome-based pricing, meaning customers only pay when such tools actually complete a task successfully or help the customers make more money. For now, Salesforce and some other software firms developing tollgates for customers' AI agents haven't started charging the tolls. They're letting customers experiment for free with the technology a little while longer. (The customers still have to pay providers such as Anthropic to use the AI agents in the first place.) Starting around November, according to the company's website, Salesforce will require customers to register any externally-made AI agents if they plan to use them to take actions on their behalf in Salesforce apps. Each action an agent takes in Salesforce counts as a billable "interaction," according to the company. The move has lifted investor confidence in Salesforce recently. Salesforce describes the registration requirement as a security measure because the company gives each agent its own identity and narrower data-access permissions, compared to humans. It isn't clear how Salesforce will clamp down on customers using their own AI agents, such as OpenClaw-powered ones that run on a person's computer and can access any app that runs on it. (Salesforce did not respond to requests for comment.) Salesforce hasn't announced prices tied to such agent usage, but customers could eventually end up paying a lot more money than they do now, given how many of them are already using their own AI on top of Salesforce apps and bypassing Salesforce's own built-in AI tools, according to software consultants and chief information officers. Nick Hamm, a software consultant, said that most of the 150 enterprises he works with are currently using AI from Anthropic and OpenAI to automate work inside Salesforce apps, for free. But they're reconsidering that usage in anticipation of the upcoming fees. If the fees are too high, the customers may move their business data outside of Salesforce's apps so they can use AI to analyze the data without paying an extra cost, he said. New customers will have a three month grace period after the new pricing is announced to register their AI agents, and the pricing won't affect existing customers until their contracts are renewed. In addition to the billable "interactions," customers have the option to buy unlimited agent usage by purchasing a "headless license," a Salesforce account executive told Hamm in a LinkedIn message viewed by The Information. Some customers such as Lumen, a fiber-optic network provider to enterprises and data centers, say they are waiting to test Salesforce's new connectors until pricing is disclosed. So far, Lumen has leaned on Salesforce's built-in AI. A longtime customer of Salesforce's customer relationship management software, Lumen made a "major" investment in using Salesforce's AI sales agents in the last 12 months, according to CIO Jim Fowler. The sales agents help with tasks such as collecting customer information and generating sales quotes for the customers to buy fiber connections between data centers, saving Lumen's human salespeople considerable time, he said. So far, Fowler said, Salesforce has been "super flexible" about letting Lumen use existing subscription fees to also cover its use of built-in AI features such as the sales agents. Early customer reactions to the pricing announcement will likely determine how flexible Salesforce is with customers that start renewing their contracts after November. If its past AI pricing efforts are any guide, Salesforce could easily switch things up depending on the feedback, or any blowback, it receives.
